record.original_question: For each integer n ≥ 0, let I_n and K_n be the modified Bessel functions arising from the modified Bessel equation r² f'' + r f' − (r²+n²)f = 0, with I_n nonsingular at zero and K_n singular at zero. For λ>0, integer l≥2, and R>0, define C_{j,λ}(R)=K'_j(R) I_j(√λ R) − √λ I'_j(√λ R) K_j(R), define C_λ(R)=√λ K_0(R) I_1(√λ R)+K_1(R) I_0(√λ R), and define F_{λ,l}(R)=l√λ R C_λ(R)[(C_{1,λ}(R)/C_{l,λ}(R)) K_l(R) I_l(√λ R) − K_1(R) I_1(√λ R)] − (1/C_λ(R))[(C_{1,λ}(R)/C_{l,λ}(R)) K_l(R) I'_l(√λ R) − K_1(R) I'_1(√λ R)]. Prove the following three claims: C_λ(R) and C_{l,λ}(R) are nonzero so F_{λ,l}(R) is well-defined for all λ>0, l≥2, and R>0; if 0<λ≤1 and l≥2 then F_{λ,l}(R) is negative and monotonically increasing for R>0; and if λ>1 and l≥2 then there exists R₁>0 such that F_{λ,l}(R) is increasing on (0,R₁), decreasing for R>R₁, and F_{λ,l}(R₁)>0.

evidence.quote: For n ≥ 0, n ∈ Z, consider the following ODE: r2 d2f dr2 + r df dr − (r2 + n2)f = 0. These ODEs are so-called modified Bessel equations. As a linear second order ODE, the solution can be written as f = c1In + c2Kn, where c1 and c2 are constants. As r → 0, In has no singularity at zero, while Kn has a singularity at zero. The functions In and Kn are called modified Bessel functions.

For λ > 0, l ≥ 2, l ∈ Z, define the function Fλ,l(R) as follows (which is a rescaled version of F4 in (Feng et al., 2023)): Fλ,l(R) = l√λR Cλ(R) ( C1,λ(R) Cl,λ(R) Kl(R)Il(√λR) − K1(R)I1(√λR) ) − 1 Cλ(R) ( C1,λ(R) Cl,λ(R) Kl(R)I′l(√λR) − K1(R)I′1(√λR) ), where Cj,λ(R) = K′j(R)Ij(√λR) − √λI′j(√λR)Kj(R), and Cλ(R) = √λK0(R)I1(√λR) + K1(R)I0(√λR), and I′j(x) = d dxIj(x), K′j(x) = d dxKj(x).

1. Verify that Fλ,l(R) is well-defined for λ > 0, l ≥ 2, and R > 0. That is, Cλ(R) and Cl,λ(R) are nonzero for R > 0. 2. If 0 < λ ≤ 1 and l ≥ 2, l ∈ Z, then Fλ,l(R) is negative and monotonically increasing for R > 0. 3. If λ > 1 and l ≥ 2, l ∈ Z, then there exists R1 > 0 such that Fλ,l(R) is increasing for R ∈ (0, R1), decreasing for R > R1, and Fλ,l(R1) > 0.

Result. QED did not produce a proof for this problem. Across all 9 rounds, QED’s own verification pipeline identified errors in every attempted proof and rejected them—the system self-verified to reject its own outputs without any human intervention.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each integer $n\ge 0$, let $I_n$ and $K_n$ denote the modified Bessel functions of the first and second kind, i.e., the two linearly independent solutions of the modified Bessel equation
$$ r^2 f''(r) + r f'(r) - (r^2 + n^2) f(r) = 0, \qquad r>0, $$
normalized so that $I_n$ is regular at $r=0$ and $K_n$ is singular at $r=0$. Write $I_n'(x) = \frac{d}{dx} I_n(x)$ and $K_n'(x) = \frac{d}{dx} K_n(x)$.

For $\lambda>0$, an integer $j\ge 0$, and $R>0$, define
$$ C_{j,\lambda}(R) = K_j'(R)\, I_j(\sqrt{\lambda}\,R) - \sqrt{\lambda}\, I_j'(\sqrt{\lambda}\,R)\, K_j(R), $$
$$ C_\lambda(R) = \sqrt{\lambda}\, K_0(R)\, I_1(\sqrt{\lambda}\,R) + K_1(R)\, I_0(\sqrt{\lambda}\,R), $$
and, for an integer $l\ge 2$,
$$ F_{\lambda,l}(R) = l\sqrt{\lambda}\, R\, C_\lambda(R) \left[ \frac{C_{1,\lambda}(R)}{C_{l,\lambda}(R)}\, K_l(R)\, I_l(\sqrt{\lambda}\,R) - K_1(R)\, I_1(\sqrt{\lambda}\,R) \right] $$
$$ - \frac{1}{C_\lambda(R)}\left[ \frac{C_{1,\lambda}(R)}{C_{l,\lambda}(R)}\, K_l(R)\, I_l'(\sqrt{\lambda}\,R) - K_1(R)\, I_1'(\sqrt{\lambda}\,R) \right]. $$

Prove the following three statements.

(a) For every $\lambda>0$, every integer $l\ge 2$, and every $R>0$, one has $C_\lambda(R)\ne 0$ and $C_{l,\lambda}(R)\ne 0$, so that $F_{\lambda,l}(R)$ is well defined.

(b) If $0<\lambda \le 1$ and $l\ge 2$ is an integer, then $F_{\lambda,l}(R) < 0$ for all $R>0$ and $F_{\lambda,l}$ is monotonically increasing on $(0,\infty)$.

(c) If $\lambda>1$ and $l\ge 2$ is an integer, then there exists $R_1>0$ such that $F_{\lambda,l}$ is increasing on $(0,R_1)$, decreasing on $(R_1,\infty)$, and $F_{\lambda,l}(R_1) > 0$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem concerns qualitative properties of a particular combination of modified Bessel functions, presented as a rescaled version of an auxiliary function appearing in prior work on a related PDE/spectral problem. No published resolution of these three claims could be confirmed through search; the status appears to remain unverified in the literature.
